hints.title: Word Independence
hints.text: Each space-separated word can be permuted independently without affecting other words.

hints.title: Multinomial Permutations
hints.text: For a word with length L and character frequencies c_i, the number of distinct anagrams is factorial of L divided by the product of factorials of each c_i.

hints.title: Modular Inverse Arithmetic
hints.text: Compute factorials and apply Fermat's Little Theorem to divide by factorials modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Word Permutations Counting Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def countAnagrams(self, s: str) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        words = s.split(' ')
        ans = 1
        for w in words:
            counts = Counter(w)
            num = math.factorial(len(w))
            den = 1
            for c in counts.values():
                den = (den * math.factorial(c)) % MOD
            ans = (ans * num * pow(den, MOD - 2, MOD)) % MOD
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Linear time frequency counting and modular arithmetic per word.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating actual anagram permutations takes factorial time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory to store split words and frequency maps.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies multinomial coefficients and modular inverse arithmetic.
